description: Computer and information systems managers plan, organize, direct, control and evaluate the activities of organizations that analyze, design, develop, implement, operate and administer computer and telecommunications software, networks and information systems. They are employed throughout the public and private sectors.
duties: This group performs some or all of the following duties:
Plan, organize, direct, control and evaluate the operations of information systems and electronic data processing (EDP) departments and companies
Develop and implement policies and procedures for electronic data processing and computer systems development and operations
Meet with clients to discuss system requirements, specifications, costs and timelines
Assemble and manage teams of information systems personnel to design, develop, implement, operate and administer computer and telecommunications software, networks and information systems
Control the budget and expenditures of the department, company or project
Recruit and supervise computer analysts, engineers, programmers, technicians and other personnel and oversee their professional development and training.
requirements: A bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, business administration, commerce or engineering is usually required.
Several years of experience in systems analysis, data administration, software engineering, network design or computer programming, including supervisory experience, are required.

drivers.name: Processing Information
drivers.reason: Compiling, classifying, coding and checking digital information offer substantial software assistance potential.

drivers.name: Planning and Organizing

drivers.name: Analyzing Data or Information

constraints.name: Supervising Subordinates
constraints.reason: Administrative supervision can be supported; responsibility, feedback and staff relationships remain human work.

constraints.name: Team Building
constraints.reason: Software can suggest activities, but building shared trust and cooperation requires people.

constraints.name: Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships
constraints.reason: Suggested messages can help, but software does not replace reciprocal human trust and relationships.

humanContext.name: Consequences of error
humanContext.reason: Higher consequences strengthen the case for human verification.

humanContext.name: Health and safety responsibility
humanContext.reason: Responsibility for people’s safety makes human oversight important.

humanContext.name: Responsibility for outcomes
humanContext.reason: Accountability for outcomes remains with people and organizations.

humanContext.name: Face-to-face discussion
humanContext.reason: Frequent in-person discussion provides context that software alone does not supply.

activities.name: Estimating Quantifiable Characteristics
activities.reason: Software can assist estimates and calculations; obtaining reliable real-world inputs still matters.

activities.name: Getting Information
activities.reason: Search, retrieval and summarization can assist gathering digital information; access and verification remain constraints.

activities.name: Identifying Objects, Actions and Events
activities.reason: Models can help classify supplied information or images, but direct observation and context are often needed.

activities.name: Inspecting Equipment, Structures or Material
activities.reason: Image or document review can assist inspection; physical access, measurement and accountability remain human work.

activities.name: Monitoring Processes, Materials or Systems
activities.reason: Software can summarize readings and flag anomalies; monitoring physical processes requires sensors and intervention.

activities.name: Controlling Machines and Processes
activities.reason: Generating instructions does not itself control or safely operate physical equipment. Robotics is outside this index.

activities.name: Developing Technical Instructions
activities.reason: Drafting, explaining and revising technical instructions are digital language tasks, with expert verification required.

activities.name: Documenting and Recording Information
activities.reason: Transcription, structured extraction and document drafting are directly addressable by generative software.

activities.name: Electronic Maintenance
activities.reason: Diagnostic advice can assist, while handling, repairing and testing equipment remain physical activities.

activities.name: Handling and Manipulating Objects
activities.reason: Software alone cannot handle physical objects. This index excludes robotics.

activities.name: Managing Resources
activities.reason: Planning and analysis can be assisted; allocating resources and accepting responsibility require organizational authority.

activities.name: Mechanical Maintenance
activities.reason: Instructions can assist troubleshooting, but software does not perform hands-on mechanical repairs.

activities.name: Operating Vehicles, Mechanized Devices or Equipment
activities.reason: Vehicle and equipment operation are outside this software-only generative AI scope.

activities.name: Performing Physical Activities
activities.reason: Bodily effort and movement cannot be performed by software alone.
